chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The creation are the dependants of Allah, so the most beloved of the creation to Allah is the one who benefits the dependants of Allah and brings joy to a family.'

key_terms.أَحَبُّ الْخَلْقِ: The most beloved of the creation

ai.seo_question: What makes a person most beloved to Allah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores the concept of 'Iyal Allah' (Allah's dependents), framing social welfare as an act of worship that mirrors divine mercy. It connects the Prophet’s teachings to the Imams' emphasis on *al-nafa'* (benefiting others) and *al-faraj* (relieving distress), establishing kindness to families as a primary criterion for divine favor. This elevates everyday social interactions to spiritual significance, reflecting the Imams' holistic view of community care.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The people are the dependants of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. Therefore, the most beloved of the people to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the one who benefits the dependants of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the most, and enters the cheerfulness upon the family members’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘The creatures are the dependents of Allah. The most beloved creature to Allah is the one who is most beneficial to Allah’s dependents (like family members) and who provides the utmost happiness to a family.’”
